title: 2006 AMC 10B Problem 19
statement: A circle of radius \(2\) is centered at \(O.\) Square \(OABC\) has side length \(1.\) Sides \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{CB}\) are extended past \(B\) to meet the circle at \(D\) and \(E,\) respectively. What is the area of the shaded region in the figure, which is bounded by \(\overline{BD},\) \(\overline{BE},\) and the minor arc connecting \(D\) and \(E?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(OA=1\) and \(OD=2\) with \(D\) on the line \(x=1,\) we get \(\angle AOD=60^\circ,\) and likewise \(\angle COE=60^\circ,\) so \(\angle DOE=30^\circ.\)

The sector \(DOE\) has area \(\tfrac{30}{360}\pi(2^2)=\tfrac{\pi}{3}.\)

The region is this sector minus triangles \(OBD\) and \(OBE.\) With \(BD=BE=\sqrt3-1,\) each triangle has area \(\tfrac12(\sqrt3-1)(1),\) totaling \(\sqrt3-1.\)

So the shaded area is \(\tfrac{\pi}{3}-(\sqrt3-1)=\tfrac{\pi}{3}+1-\sqrt3.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Shaded area equals sector \(DOE\) minus the two right triangles \(OBD\) and \(OBE\)
